capitals.name: Sa`dah (Saada)
capitals.note: 'Houthi fighters entered Saada on March 19' 2011, took the city on 24 March and set up their own administration in the governorate on 26 March.

capitals.name: Sanaa
capitals.note: The Houthis took Sanaa in September 2014; on 6 February 2015 'the Revolutionary Committee' became the acting authority (Houthis page); the war page says they 'currently control the capital Sanaa'.

The Marib page has government forces establishing control over 'the eastern and western regions of Marib province' in September 2015 and recapturing Marib 'by late 2016', so all of Ma'rib is left out to 2021. The page calls the 10 September 2026 taking of Mokha a recapture without saying when it was lost; Mokha is left out from 2015 (confidence 1). The Taiz, Hodeidah and Aden fronts are not dated by any page opened and are not drawn.

ledger.note: Late 2011: Al Jawf. Fighting began on 8 July after the governor fled and 'over 120 people were killed' by 28 July; it lasted about four months and 'the Houthis eventually took control of al-Jawf governorate'. The page gives no month for the end.

19-26 March 2011: the Houthis set up their own administration in Sa`dah. 'Houthi fighters entered Saada on March 19', took the city on 24 March after the governor fled, and on 26 March 'declared the creation of their own administration in Saada Governorate, independent from Yemeni authorities'.

region.text: Hajjah Governorate, taken from the north

ledger.note: 9 November 2011: northern Hajjah. The Houthis 'broke through pro-government tribal lines', took Kuhlan Ash Sharaf District and advanced toward the port of Midi, 'sea access and control of the road linking Sanaa to the coast'. The Houthis page says 'most of' Hajjah in May 2012; the whole governorate is the researcher's reading.

September-October 2012: round Sanaa. Protests and clashes led to 'the Houthis expanding their control in Sanaa Governorate and other areas around the capital' (Khwlan and Sanhan districts, Shibam Kawkaban in al-Mahwit). The page gives no extent.

region.text: Amran Governorate, between Sa`dah and Sanaa

ledger.note: 2014: Amran Governorate. Bridging, confidence 1: no page opened dates its capture; the Houthis had a school at Shaharah in December 2011 and withdrew from Raydah in September 2012 after a ceasefire.

21 September 2014: the Houthis take Sanaa. 'On 21 September, as the Houthis took control of Sanaa, the Yemeni Army did not formally intervene' and a UN-brokered unity-government deal was signed that day; the war page has 'Houthi fighters seized control of Sanaa'. Sanaa Governorate is the researcher's addition (fighting spread there 'by mid-2014').

6 February 2015: the Houthis rule from Sanaa. 'The movement officially took control of the government, dissolved parliament, and declared its Revolutionary Committee the acting authority'; Mohammed Ali al-Houthi became acting president.

ledger.note: 6 February 2015: 'the group was taking control of the country'. The page names no governorates; the researcher reads the extent from the war page's present-day sentence ('all of former North Yemen except for eastern Marib Governorate'), minus Ma'rib, where the government is in control from September 2015.

25 March 2015: the Houthis reach Aden. 'By 25 March, Lahij fell to the Houthis and they reached the outskirts of Aden'; Hadi fled the country the same day; Saudi-led airstrikes began on 27 March (Houthis page).

22 July 2015: the Battle of Aden ends. 'The Battle of Aden lasted four months' (25 March-22 July 2015, Houthis page). The pages opened do not say who won; the Houthis hold nothing south of former North Yemen on the present-day sentence, so Lahij and Aden are not Houthi.

13 November 2020: the Houthis announce the capture of Camp Mas, 'which could open the way to the Raghwan and Midghal districts'; an earlier claim of advances in Mahliyah district (1 September 2020) was denied by the government.
1 April 2022: a UN-sponsored two-month nationwide truce begins and 'continued in practice' until October 2022 (Marib page); the war page dates it 2 April. The front at Marib stays where it was.

minus.text: Ma'rib Governorate east of about 45.18 E, 10-20 km west of Marib city: the 'eastern Marib' the page leaves out

ledger.note: April 2022: the truce fixes the Houthi hold on western Marib. The war page puts the Houthis in all of former North Yemen 'except for eastern Marib Governorate' but gives no date for the taking; the truce date is the latest the line can have been drawn (confidence 1).
10 September 2026: 'The Houthis recaptured Mokha'. The page does not say when the Houthis lost it or who held it.

region.text: Perim Island and the Hanish Islands

ledger.note: 11 September 2026: 'The Houthis recaptured Perim Island and then the Hanish Islands, completing their seizure of the Red Sea coast.'

wars.name: Houthi insurgency (2011 to 2014 phase)

zones.text: Sa`dah, Al Jawf, Hajjah and the districts round Sanaa

wars.outcome: From the 2004 insurgency (18 June 2004 to the 2010 ceasefire, Houthis page) to March 2011, when the Houthis took Saada and declared their own administration; by November 2011 they held Al Jawf and northern Hajjah; they took Sanaa on 21 September 2014.
wars.note: Only the part from 2011 is inside the state life; the 2004-2010 war carries no dated land on the pages opened.

wars.name: Yemeni civil war

zones.text: former North Yemen against the internationally recognised government

wars.outcome: From the Houthi takeover of Sanaa in September 2014; the Saudi-led coalition intervened on 27 March 2015; a UN truce began on 2 April 2022; on 7 April 2022 the Hadi government was dissolved in favour of a Presidential Leadership Council; the Houthis took Mokha, Perim and the Hanish Islands on 10-11 September 2026.
wars.note: The war article was opened for dated changes only; its front lines at Taiz, Hodeidah and the west coast are not dated there.

wars.name: Marib campaign
wars.outcome: Camp Mas 13 November 2020; the offensive renewed 7-8 February 2021; claims of al-Abdiyah on 17 October 2021 (title only); a UN truce on 1 April 2022.
wars.note: The page covers Marib from September 2015; the Shabwa districts of late 2021 and the Giants Brigades are not on it.

certainty.note: An insurgency's de facto control with no survey line: the governorate shapes are administrative proxies; the Marib, Taiz, Hodeidah and west-coast fronts moved without dates on the pages opened and are not drawn.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (its Yemen rows draw the whole country); republic-of-yemen's 2014-09 contest_start names this slug and draws all of former North Yemen except Ma'rib as contested from 2014, so this dossier and that one should be read together: the Houthi keyframes show who holds the land, the Yemeni contest event blends the colours. Written by me-10-x; 5 pages opened (budget up to 5), no more. Not opened: the Houthi insurgency Sa'dah war pages 2004-2010, the Battle of Aden, Taiz, Hodeidah offensive and Stockholm Agreement pages, the Supreme Political Council page; none of Amran 2014, Dhamar, Ibb, Hodeidah or the Taiz siege is dated on a page opened. Page conflicts: the war page's sentence that the Houthis hold 'all of former North Yemen except for eastern Marib' contradicts its own September 2026 'recaptured Mokha'; the dossier follows the dated events and subtracts the Mokha district from 2015. The Saleh alliance and split (2 and 4 December 2017) and the Supreme Political Council have no land in the pages opened. The gazetteer lacks Mokha, Perim and the Hanish Islands (lon/lat radii used). Typed rebel because the state is unrecognised; the Sanaa authorities call themselves the government. Ongoing: end year 2026 is the current year, no dissolve.
